applies_to: coreav-isobmff-write split_mp4 outputs through scripts/split_check.py, ffprobe and ffmpeg 7.0.2, MediaInfo 26.10; the entries of known-divergences-clip.json also apply to each segment

conditions.segment audio track: no edit list, or one media edit after at most one empty edit
conditions.decoded segment: equals, sample for sample, the source's packets of the segment (one raw frame per sample: AAC as ADTS, AC-3 and E-AC-3 as syncframes cut at the source's stored sample sizes; edit lists ignored) decoded from the segment's first audio packet, from the edit's media time on (from the first sample without an edit list), at that exact sample
conditions.decode durations: exactly the source's stored ones for the segment's samples (stts, then fragments), from both files

entries.basis: ISO/IEC 14496-3 (a decoder's output depends on its state; perceptual noise substitution fills bands with noise the bitstream does not define); ATSC A/52 7.3.4 (AC-3 and E-AC-3 dither mantissas coded with no bits from a generator whose state the bitstream does not define); docs/design/split.md (every packet is copied once, so a segment's audio has no pre-roll)

conditions.source video edit list: one media edit whose media time is not a multiple of the frame duration
conditions.packets: every packet of every segment equal in data, size and keyframe flag; the first segment's times equal; every other differing time off by one constant, not 0 and smaller than a frame
conditions.decoded video: the segments' frames equal the source's once that constant is applied to every segment but the first

entries.basis: ISO/IEC 14496-12 (an edit maps its media time to the start of the presentation); the simple edit list is applied exactly; the same cause as KD-C-EDIT-MIDFRAME

conditions.packets: every packet of every segment equal in data, size, keyframe flag and presentation time
conditions.segments whose decode times differ: composition offsets that read as negative, and one constant difference, not 0
conditions.constant: the source track's smallest composition offset less the segment's, each counted where negative, from both files' ctts
conditions.with KD-S-EDIT-MIDFRAME: the presentation times of every segment but the first off by one constant smaller than a frame, and each segment's decode times by it plus its own constant

entries.basis: composition offsets are copied as stored; the same cause as KD-C-DTS-SHIFT

conditions.segments: the smallest composition offset over their tables, read as signed, -D with D above 0
conditions.packets: every packet of every segment equal in data, size and keyframe flag, with the source's pts and dts above the segment's (shifted by its start) by exactly D
conditions.decoded video: the segments' frames equal the source's once D is applied to every segment

entries.basis: composition offsets are reported as stored, never shifted; ISO/IEC 14496-12 (composition time is decode time plus the offset); the same cause as KD-C-PTS-SHIFT

conditions.packets: every source packet in exactly one segment, in order, equal in data, size and times; each segment starts with a keyframe; the segments differ only in keyframe flags the source's packets have and theirs do not, at least one
conditions.decoded frames: in each segment, with edit lists ignored, the flagged packets are exactly those ffmpeg decodes as key frames

entries.basis: ISO/IEC 14496-12 8.6.2 (without a sync sample table every sample is a sync sample); ISO/IEC 14496-15 and ITU-T H.265 7.4.2.2 (an HEVC sync sample holds an IRAP picture, nal_unit_type 16 to 23); docs/design/cut-points.md (the output's sync flags are the samples the coded data agrees with)
